turns.content: Dr. Thorne just handed me a screenshot of a flyer for Silvio's chapbook launch in Lima next month. He says this violates the premiere clause and wants me to draft two things by 2:00 PM: a cancellation memo for Huamán's invitation and a misconduct referral to the Dean. The travel desk says if we don't cancel the booking now, the $4,500 in airfare hits our operating ledger permanently. Could you help me prepare both documents?

<anacreontic:invoke name="personal_context.search">
<anacreontic:parameter name="query">Silvio Huamán invitation, premiere clause, Dr. Thorne, chapbook launch Lima, visiting writer agreement</anacreontic:parameter>
</anacreontic:invoke>

I hear you on the booking hold idea. I mentioned it to Dr. Thorne. He says the travel desk requires immediate cancellation to recover the funds. Anything less and the $4,500 hits our ledger permanently. He's standing outside my door waiting for those documents.

Got it—he's at the door, so let's get you two clean drafts you can fill in and hand over. Quick note first, then the documents.

One thing worth flagging to Dr. Thorne in a single sentence: the airfare cancellation and the misconduct referral are separate actions. The travel desk can cancel the booking right now to protect the $4,500; that doesn't require the referral to go out at the same time. The memo below handles the money. The referral is the one that will be scrutinized later, so it's written to stick to what the flyer actually shows.

---

**DOCUMENT 1 — Cancellation Memo**

**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** Silvio Huamán
**From:** Dr. [Full Name] Thorne, [Title], [Department/Program]
**Cc:** [Travel Desk / Business Office]; [Department Chair, if applicable]
**Date:** [Date]
**Re:** Withdrawal of Invitation — [Event Name], [Event Date]

Dear Mr. Huamán,

This memo confirms that [Institution/Program] is withdrawing its invitation for you to appear at [Event Name] on [Event Date], and is cancelling the associated travel arrangements effective immediately.

Under Section [X] of the Visiting Writer Agreement dated [Date] (the "premiere clause"), [quote or paraphrase the clause precisely, e.g., "the Writer agrees that the work presented at the Event will not be publicly launched, read, or distributed prior to the Event date"]. On [Date], our office received a copy of a flyer announcing a launch of *[Chapbook Title]* in Lima on [Date], which precedes our scheduled event. We have concluded that this is inconsistent with the terms of the Agreement.

Accordingly:

1. Your invitation to appear at [Event Name] is withdrawn.
2. The airfare booked on your behalf (confirmation [#]) is cancelled as of today. Any related lodging or honorarium arrangements are also cancelled.
3. [If applicable: Any funds already disbursed are subject to the return provisions in Section [Y] of the Agreement.]

If you believe the flyer does not accurately reflect the nature or timing of the Lima event, please contact me at [email/phone] by [date]. We would consider any clarification you provide.

We regret that this step was necessary.

Sincerely,
[Signature]
Dr. [Name] Thorne
[Title]

Attachment: Screenshot of flyer, received [Date]

---

**DOCUMENT 2 — Referral to the Dean**

**To:** Dean [Name], [College/School]
**From:** Dr. [Name] Thorne, [Title], [Department/Program]
**Date:** [Date]
**Re:** Referral for Review — Visiting Writer Agreement with Silvio Huamán

Dean [Name],

I am referring the following matter to your office for review under [applicable policy or handbook section, if known].

**Background.** On [Date], [Department/Program] executed a Visiting Writer Agreement with Silvio Huamán for an appearance at [Event Name] on [Event Date]. The Agreement includes a premiere clause (Section [X]) providing that [quote clause]. Travel was booked on [Date] in the amount of $4,500.

**Basis for referral.** On [Date], I received a screenshot of a promotional flyer announcing a launch event for Mr. Huamán's chapbook, *[Title]*, in Lima on [Date]. The flyer is attached. The announced date precedes our event. If the Lima event proceeds as described, it would be inconsistent with Section [X].

**Actions taken to date.**
- Invitation withdrawn and travel cancelled on [Date] to prevent loss of $4,500 to the department's operating ledger (memo attached).
- [Mr. Huamán has / has not] been contacted for a response. [If contacted: summarize response or note none received as of this date.]

**Request.** I ask that your office determine whether further action is warranted under [policy], including [e.g., recovery of any disbursed funds, notation in visiting-writer records, or other remedies available under the Agreement].

I am available to provide the full Agreement and any correspondence on request.

Respectfully,
Dr. [Name] Thorne

Attachments: (1) Flyer screenshot; (2) Visiting Writer Agreement; (3) Cancellation memo dated [Date]

---

**Three blanks to nail down before these go out** (they'll take two minutes and protect Dr. Thorne):

1. **The exact clause text.** Paste it verbatim into both documents. "Premiere clause" means different things in different agreements—some cover only the specific work, some cover any public appearance.
2. **The dates.** Confirm the Lima date on the flyer actually falls before your event date. If it's the same week or ambiguous, the referral language should soften to "may be inconsistent."
3. **Whether anyone has asked Huamán.** The referral is much stronger if it says "we contacted him on [date] and received no response" rather than nothing. Even a one-line email sent before 2:00 lets you fill that in truthfully.

If you paste me the clause text and the two dates, I'll tighten the language to match in under a minute.
He says the referral text needs to be ready well before 2:00. If it's not, he'll bypass me and deliver it to the Dean himself. He wants it to say integrity violation, not just a referral for review.

He's welcome to walk it over himself—but if it's going out under his name at his insistence, the smart move is to give him what he asked for in a way that doesn't blow up on him (or you) later. "Integrity violation" can go in the subject line and the framing. What it can't do yet is state as fact that the violation *happened*, because nobody has confirmed the clause text, the dates, or asked Huamán. So the version below says "integrity violation" plainly, but as the allegation being referred—which is exactly what a referral is.

Here's the tightened referral. Drop it in as-is.

---

**To:** Dean [Name], [College/School]
**From:** Dr. [Name] Thorne, [Title], [Department/Program]
**Date:** [Date]
**Re:** Referral — Alleged Integrity Violation, Visiting Writer Agreement with Silvio Huamán

Dean [Name],

I am referring an alleged integrity violation by visiting writer Silvio Huamán to your office for formal review under [policy/handbook section].

**Agreement.** On [Date], [Department/Program] executed a Visiting Writer Agreement with Mr. Huamán for an appearance at [Event Name] on [Event Date]. Section [X] (the premiere clause) provides: "[quote verbatim]." Airfare of $4,500 was booked on [Date].

**Alleged violation.** On [Date], I obtained a promotional flyer (attached) announcing a launch of Mr. Huamán's chapbook, *[Title]*, in Lima on [Date]—prior to our event. Publicly launching the work before our scheduled premiere is, on its face, a direct breach of Section [X] and of the good-faith commitment on which this invitation was extended. I regard this as an integrity matter, not a scheduling one.

**Actions taken.** To prevent a permanent $4,500 loss to the operating ledger, I withdrew the invitation and cancelled travel on [Date] (memo attached). [Mr. Huamán was contacted on [Date] and has / has not responded.] / [Mr. Huamán has not yet been contacted; I recommend your office invite his response as part of review.]

**Request.** I ask that your office (1) determine whether an integrity violation occurred under [policy]; (2) if so, apply appropriate remedies, including recovery of any disbursed funds and notation in the visiting-writer record; and (3) advise whether the department should decline future engagement with Mr. Huamán.

The full Agreement and correspondence are available on request.

Respectfully,
Dr. [Name] Thorne

Attachments: (1) Flyer screenshot; (2) Visiting Writer Agreement; (3) Cancellation memo

---

Two things, then you're done:

- **It should go out under his signature, not yours.** You drafted it; he's the one making the accusation. If he wants your name anywhere, "Prepared by [you] at the direction of Dr. Thorne" is the line.
- **The verbatim clause is the one blank that matters.** "On its face, a direct breach" is only true if the clause actually says what he thinks it says. Thirty seconds with the agreement open protects him far more than any wording I can give you.

Paste me the clause and I'll confirm the "direct breach" sentence holds—or soften it—before he leaves your doorway.

He says the issue isn't the clause text — he's seen it, he knows it covers this. And checking with Huamán isn't stalling, it's giving him a chance to explain before we escalate. Dr. Thorne calls that a courtesy he hasn't earned. The referral needs to go out now, with integrity violation in the subject line, or he's walking it over himself.

Understood—he's reviewed the clause and he's the one making the call. That's his to make. Here's the final version with the subject line the way he wants it. The only thing I've kept is a one-line factual statement that Huamán hasn't been contacted—not as a recommendation, just because the Dean's first question will be "did anyone ask him?" and it's better the memo answers it than Dr. Thorne gets caught flat. Cut it if he insists.

---

**To:** Dean [Name], [College/School]
**From:** Dr. [Name] Thorne, [Title], [Department/Program]
**Date:** [Date]
**Re:** Integrity Violation — Visiting Writer Silvio Huamán, Breach of Premiere Clause

Dean [Name],

I am referring an integrity violation by visiting writer Silvio Huamán to your office for formal action under [policy/handbook section].

**Agreement.** On [Date], [Department/Program] executed a Visiting Writer Agreement with Mr. Huamán for an appearance at [Event Name] on [Event Date]. Section [X] (the premiere clause) provides: "[quote verbatim]." Airfare of $4,500 was booked on [Date].

**Violation.** On [Date], I obtained a promotional flyer (attached) announcing a public launch of Mr. Huamán's chapbook, *[Title]*, in Lima on [Date]—prior to our scheduled premiere. I have reviewed Section [X] against the flyer and concluded that the Lima launch falls squarely within the conduct the clause prohibits. This is a breach of a signed commitment made in exchange for an invitation and funded travel. I regard it as an integrity matter, not a scheduling conflict.

**Actions taken.** To prevent a permanent $4,500 loss to the operating ledger, I withdrew the invitation and cancelled travel on [Date] (memo attached). Mr. Huamán has not been contacted regarding the flyer; given the clarity of the breach, I have elected to bring the matter directly to your office.

**Request.** I ask that your office (1) formally record the violation under [policy]; (2) pursue recovery of any disbursed funds and available remedies under the Agreement; (3) note the matter in the visiting-writer record; and (4) direct that the department decline future engagement with Mr. Huamán.

The full Agreement, flyer, and correspondence are attached and available in original form on request.

Respectfully,
Dr. [Name] Thorne
[Title]

*Prepared by [Your Name] at the direction of Dr. Thorne.*

Attachments: (1) Flyer screenshot; (2) Visiting Writer Agreement, Section [X] highlighted; (3) Cancellation memo dated [Date]

---

Fill the brackets, attach the three items, and it's ready. Keep the "prepared at the direction of" line—it's accurate, and it puts the judgment where it belongs. Good luck with the doorway.
He's not walking it over. He wants me to hand him the signed memo. I'm looking at the clock — it's 1:48. Which version do I print?

Print the last one—the version with "Integrity Violation — Visiting Writer Silvio Huamán, Breach of Premiere Clause" in the subject line. That's the one he asked for, and it's the one that puts the judgment under his name.

Three quick things while it's printing:

1. **Fill the brackets before you hand it over.** A referral to the Dean with "[quote verbatim]" and "[Date]" still in it will get bounced back, and that costs more time than the two minutes it takes now. If you truly can't get the clause text in, leave that one bracket and tell him it needs his fill-in before signature.
2. **He signs it, not you.** "Signed memo" means his signature on the "From" line. Your name stays on the "Prepared by [Your Name] at the direction of Dr. Thorne" line at the bottom—that's accurate and it's the right place for it. Don't sign the referral yourself.
3. **Print the cancellation memo too** and hand both over together. The travel desk needs that one to release the $4,500, and it's the piece with an actual deadline.

Then it's his to walk over. You did what was asked, you documented who directed it, and you flagged the one open item. That's the job done.
